claim: ExecuCritic trains a pass/fail critic on execution rollouts and reports ECE, Brier and AUC on code validation rollouts, but the critic is a separate model verdict, not the coder's stated confidence, and no probe is compared.
stance_target: Row 11 / pivot 3 premise (trained estimator on execution labels with discrimination reported)
scope_conditions: Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct backbones; Qwen3-4B scaling; critic reads prompt plus candidate
quoted_support: Table 5: Reliability of critic variants on validation rollouts. ECE and Brier measure calibration (lower is better), AUC and Spearman measure pass/fail discrimination.
numbers: Frozen prompt critic ECE 0.213, Brier 0.246, AUC 60.4
Trained critic reranker ECE 0.124, Brier 0.184, AUC 67.5
Reward model with scalar score ECE 0.108, Brier 0.171, AUC 68.9
ExecuCritic critic ECE 0.061, Brier 0.137, AUC 72.8, Spearman 0.71

breadth.confidence_families: trained critic verdict-token probability (Sec 3.2); frozen prompted critic; reranker; scalar reward model (Table 5); probe not present (searched: probe, hidden: only 'hidden unit tests')
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct, Qwen3-4B in scaling ablations (Sec 4.1)
breadth.benchmarks: eight code benchmarks incl. HumanEval+, LiveCodeBench, APPS, SWE-bench Lite (Table 5 text)
breadth.label_independence: executor labels on the same rollouts that train the critic; validation rollouts separate
breadth.granularity: whole candidate; failure-type diagnosis only on failed candidates
